name: Colin Powell
role: US Army general, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff and Secretary of State (1937-2021)
summary: Colin Powell, a retired Army general who chaired the Joint Chiefs and served as George W. Bush's Secretary of State, was a moderate Republican who supported abortion rights and affirmative action, argued the 2003 case against Iraq at the UN, and endorsed Barack Obama in 2008.

sources.title: CNN Special Event: Colin Powell's speech to the 2000 Republican National Convention (31 July 2000), transcript via the MediaSum corpus
sources.author: Colin Powell
sources.usedFor: 'I believe in a woman's right to choose, and I strongly support affirmative action.'

sources.title: CNN TalkBack Live (1 August 2000), transcript via the MediaSum corpus
sources.author: Colin Powell
sources.usedFor: The Republican convention remarks on affirmative action and the black community.

sources.title: NPR Morning Edition: Powell: Don't Let Terrorism Change 'Who We Are' (2 September 2011), transcript via the MediaSum corpus
sources.author: Colin Powell
sources.usedFor: Government's responsibility for citizens in need of health care; immigration and an open, welcoming America; civilian courts versus Guantanamo.

sources.title: UN Security Council meeting S/PV.4701 (5 February 2003), Powell's presentation on Iraq, via the UN Security Council Debates corpus
sources.author: Colin Powell
sources.usedFor: Resolution 1441, the Council's duty to see its resolutions complied with and the risk of irrelevance.

sources.title: Crisis in Darfur: hearing before the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations (9 September 2004), CHRG-108shrg97822, via the local hearings corpus
sources.author: Colin Powell, Secretary of State
sources.usedFor: His determination: 'we concluded, I concluded, that genocide has been committed in Darfur'.

sources.title: Powell Supports Repeal of Don't Ask, Don't Tell, The Advocate (3 February 2010)
sources.author: Kerry Eleveld (reporting a statement by Colin Powell)
sources.usedFor: He 'helped craft the policy in 1993 when he chaired the Joint Chiefs of Staff'; his 2010 statement that 'attitudes and circumstances have changed'.

sources.title: Nomination of Colin L. Powell to be Secretary of State: hearing before the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations (17 January 2001), CHRG-107shrg71536, via the local hearings corpus
sources.author: Colin Powell
sources.usedFor: His opening statement: democracy and capitalism as the two most important ideas, sanctions on Iraq, the Taiwan balance, Vietnam's lesson.

sources.title: Treaty on Strategic Offensive Reductions (Moscow Treaty): hearing before the Senate Committee on Foreign Relations (2002), CHRG-107shrg81339, via the local hearings corpus
sources.author: Colin Powell, Secretary of State
sources.usedFor: His testimony in support of the Moscow Treaty's deep reductions, speaking for the administration.

sources.title: Colin Powell, Wikipedia
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of his career; no answer rests on it.

notFound.work: My American Journey (1995), It Worked for Me (2012), and his Senate testimony as Secretary of State

tried.how: searched by name: no files or hits
only lending-library scans and excerpts; no open full text

notes: First audit. MediaSum's CNN and NPR transcripts of his speeches and interviews (2000-2011) and the UN Security Council corpus (four 2003 meetings) were searched by theme: affirmative action, abortion, gays in the military, weapons of mass destruction and Iraq, death penalty, guns, immigration, Israel, taxes, health care, Vietnam, drugs, NATO, China, climate, torture, Guantanamo. As Secretary of State his statements often state the administration's line, so they are used only where they state his own position; Statements he made in office are used where he states them in his own voice (rationales say when he speaks for the administration, with medium confidence). The January 2001 confirmation hearing, the Moscow Treaty hearing and the September 2004 Darfur hearing (hearings corpus) were read by theme; the Iraq and terrorism hearings were searched (UN, coalition, regime change, Geneva) and his statements there state administration policy that settles no statement. His books are not open (notFound).
